title: one offer gets the *market test*
dek: An evidence-safe comparison of The Angle Map and the God Agent hypothesis, ending in one problem-qualified segment, one personally valuable proof object, and one bounded message-market-fit test.
lens: customer truth · problem qualification · message-market fit
sources: canonical offer records · pipeline · public company evidence

sections.heading: the verdict
sections.body:
Test The Angle Map now. It has a fixed transaction, bounded delivery, an observable target universe, and explicit commercial counters. It is still market-untested: the canonical state is 0 sent, 0 held, 0 sold, and $0 collected.

Do not run the God Agent as a co-equal public offer. The capability is real, but no external installation, customer usage, reference, outcome, or willingness-to-pay receipt exists. Its honest next state is a narrow warm proof install after the active revenue test, not another public acquisition lane.

rows.claim: The Angle Map has a complete transaction
rows.evidence: $750 prepaid, one live read, three evidence-bounded campaign angles, and a 48-hour delivery clock after readiness and payment.

rows.claim: The Angle Map does not yet have demand proof
rows.evidence: The canonical pipeline and cash scoreboard record zero sends, held conversations, sales, and collections.

rows.claim: Public company events make a candidate universe enumerable
rows.evidence: Distribution, reformulation, new-product, and retail events reveal companies with a time-bound messaging occasion, but do not prove internal pain.

rows.claim: The God Agent has capability proof but no external buyer proof
rows.evidence: The internal harness and extracted architecture are substantial. No external installation, reference customer, usage event, business outcome, or payment receipt appears in the available record.

sections.heading: the problem-qualified segment
sections.dek: The observable trigger is strong enough to test. The experienced consequence still belongs in UNKNOWN.

items.why: Established supplement, functional-beverage, recovery, or performance brands with a real product and a live market occasion inside 90 days.
Several plausible message directions, usable evidence and claim boundaries, one decision deadline, and authority to spend $750.
Founder, CEO, brand lead, or marketing owner responsible for choosing the campaign argument and able to supply the final decision-maker.
The team funds more creative before settling which buyer belief and approved proof should organize the campaign.

blocks.text:

Want me to send it?

sections.heading: promote, iterate, or kill
sections.dek: The test diagnoses qualification, value, and language separately.

items.why: At least 2 of 5 meaningful responses and at least 1 direct problem confirmation. This is message evidence, not demand proof.
One qualified buyer accepts the unchanged $750 scope and cleared money is recorded.
Replies rejecting the problem repair qualification; problem recognition without note requests repairs value; misunderstanding repairs language.
Ten qualified exposures plus permitted follow-up produce zero problem confirmations.

sections.heading: what this does not prove
sections.body: Public launch language does not reveal internal disagreement, urgency, budget, or willingness to pay. Prepared messages are not exposures. Local capability is not customer adoption. Compliments and AI curiosity are not problem confirmation. The current test remains NO PERMISSION until Farrice separately authorizes outreach.
